overview.oneLineTake: Hot inflation and a 5% 10-year yield have the Fed hiking again, and with Nvidia scandal risk on top, premium sellers should expect wider swings.
themes: Hot October CPI is pushing December Fed hike odds higher. The 10-year yield is back near 5%, and Waller's comments added to rate hike expectations.
Equities slipped Tuesday: QQQ closed 674.76 (-0.68%) and SPY 749.92 (-0.37%), ending the post-election rebound.
Nvidia fell for a second day (about -5.5%) on the Jensen Huang spy scandal, with export rule and subpoena risk ahead of earnings. Some chip dip buyers stepped in.
CoreWeave beat on revenue and raised guidance, easing AI slowdown worries. Anthropic set its IPO range at $70 to $78, with trading expected Nov 19.
Brent briefly dipped below $90 on Iran hopes and US gasoline fell below $4, a partial offset to the inflation picture.
risks: A December rate hike repricing with the 10-year at 5% is the main threat to equity multiples.
Nvidia headline risk: a probe, possible subpoenas and tougher China export rules could hit the whole AI complex.
Dow swings of 1,000 points in a day have happened three times in four days, so gap risk is elevated.
Tariffs continue despite the midterm backlash, and a record $1.29T of credit card debt adds consumer strain.

intelligence.headline: Falling Oil Prices and Bond Yields Offer Investors Some Relief
intelligence.summary: Brent crude, near $118 as recently as Oct. 30, has dropped below $90, helping pull the US 10-year Treasury yield down to 4.89% from a 24-year high around 5.36% a month ago. Economists expect today's US CPI to show inflation moderated last month, which together with cheaper oil could lead traders to pare Fed tightening bets, a backdrop that would support equities and has European stocks on the verge of a first record since August, after last week's midterm drubbing of Donald Trump and US-Iran diplomatic efforts. intelligence.headline: Fed's Waller Backs December Rate Hike, Open to Larger Move
intelligence.summary: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he supports an interest-rate hike in December and warned he would back a half-point increase if inflation continues to accelerate.

intelligence.headline: Stock Rebound Ran Out of Steam After Waller Comments
intelligence.summary: A powerful rebound in US stocks ran out of steam after Waller's comments, which come just hours before Tuesday's inflation data.

intelligence.headline: Anthropic Set to Kick Off IPO Marketing
intelligence.summary: Anthropic is set to kick off the marketing of its blockbuster IPO as early as today, with a snafu over the filing documents adding a dose of drama.

intelligence.headline: SoftBank Reports First Loss in Almost Two Years
intelligence.summary: SoftBank reported its first loss in almost two years after a $3.7 billion writedown over its US data-center projects.

intelligence.headline: On the Move: Nvidia, Take-Two, Infineon
intelligence.summary: Nvidia gains 0.3% in premarket trading, a day after investors wiped more than $190 billion in market value as a spy scandal burst into the open; Take-Two Interactive Software rises 3.1% after giving an outlook seen as conservative ahead of Grand Theft Auto VI; Infineon gains 5.4% in Frankfurt after the German chipmaker raised its 2027 data center sales forecast; Sea and Venture Global are slated to report before the open, while CoreWeave reports after the close.

intelligence.headline: The Anti-AI Trade
intelligence.summary: With Taiwan Semiconductor, Samsung and SK Hynix slumping, emerging-market fund managers are shifting toward stocks at rock-bottom valuations with high dividend yields, in markets that by one metric are the cheapest since the global financial crisis 18 years ago, highlighting South American utilities, Chinese and Taiwanese consumer-goods manufacturers, and eastern and central European financial firms. Sat Duhra at Janus Henderson Investors said concentrating in three or four names "doesn't work over the long term."

intelligence.headline: Word from Wall Street: Yields Won't Peak Until a Recession
intelligence.summary: Arif Husain, T. Rowe Price's head of global fixed income, said "Yields won't truly peak until there is a recession" and that there is a chance the Fed could hike until something breaks, arguing the Fed may have to raise rates above the level markets are currently pricing to keep inflation in check.

intelligence.headline: Poll: Tech Losses Seen Contained or Deferred to 2027
intelligence.summary: A majority of respondents to an instant poll conducted Friday through Monday, after last week's steep selloff, said tech stock losses will remain contained in the foreseeable future, or a deeper slide won't happen until 2027.
